Apple CEO John Ternus met privately with software chief Craig Federighi and pushed him to speed up Apple's AI plans, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports.
Ternus wants more than Siri fixes. Gurman says he privately admits Apple is far behind rivals.
Apple's research spending jumped 32% this year.

paragraphs.text: Apple chief executive John Ternus has pressed software chief Craig Federighi to accelerate the company's software road map and move beyond making necessary improvements to Siri, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported on November 8, 2026. According to the report, as summarized by 9to5Mac, Ternus held a closed-door meeting with Federighi in recent weeks.

Gurman wrote that Ternus is frustrated by what the report calls a reluctance to embrace AI with the same urgency as competitors. Federighi became the head of Apple's AI work after the dismissal of the company's former AI leader last year, and FourWeekMBA noted that Gurman describes him as carrying a reputation for having been an AI skeptic.

On Apple's recent earnings call, Ternus said the company now has the kind of Siri it always wanted, describing a system that is mostly request based today but built on an architecture that leaves room to grow. Gurman reported that Ternus has privately acknowledged Apple remains far behind its rivals. The new Siri models are based on technology Apple licenses from Google, according to Gurman.

Gurman also pointed to a specific gap. OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude already offer Computer Use, which lets the assistant operate a computer to complete tasks, and Apple has announced nothing comparable. Gurman wrote that he believes Apple could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year.

The report describes Federighi as taking a hands-on role in meetings and major decisions, with some team members feeling they have limited influence over product direction. He typically plans on a 12 to 18 month timeframe, compared with the multiyear road maps used in hardware. Apple is also testing a new development process that gives engineers 50% more time to write code as coding agents have improved, according to 9to5Mac.

Gurman reported that Mike Rockwell, the Vision Pro creator who now leads Siri engineering, continues to seriously consider stepping down, possibly next year, after the two-year delay in bringing the new Siri to market. Federighi has shown no sign of leaving.

Apple's spending is rising. Its fiscal 2026 annual report, filed on November 3, shows research and development costs up 32% to $45.8 billion, which the company attributed primarily to higher infrastructure costs, including investments in artificial intelligence, according to FourWeekMBA's review of the filing.

The report suggests the new chief executive sees the pace of Apple's AI work as a leadership issue rather than a budget issue, since spending is already climbing quickly. Pressing the executive who controls software, while the head of Siri weighs leaving, puts the outcome largely on how Federighi responds.

Gurman expects Siri control inside Apple's own apps as early as December and third-party app support around spring. Whether Apple adds an agent or Computer Use feature next year will show if the push is working.
